reading.title: A Snowy Saturday
reading.purpose: Listen in as a girl and her dad use word-root words while she rests at home.
paras: On a snowy Saturday, Lina woke up with a scratchy throat. Her dad put a thermometer under her tongue to measure her temperature. "Ninety-nine point one," he read. "That is not a real fever, but you should stay warm." He turned the thermostat up two degrees and brought her a thermal blanket.

"Can I at least read?" asked Lina. She pulled out a graphic biography about a famous scientist. "It tells her whole life in drawings," she said. "A biography is a true story about a person, written by someone else, but this one looks like a comic."

"Who is she?" asked Dad. "A scientist who studied fish in rivers and lakes," said Lina. "They are aquatic animals, so they spend their lives in water. I want to study biology too. It is the science of living things."

"Then let us visit the aquarium when you feel better," said Dad. "It keeps hundreds of fish in big tanks. On the way, I will show you an old aqueduct. It carried water into town long before anyone had pipes."
Lina grinned. "Last year the author of this book signed my copy. Look, here is her autograph, right on the first page!" Dad smiled. "Keep that signature safe. Now drink your tea and rest."

choices: found only in tanks at a science museum
studied only by scientists with special tools
kept safe by a scientist in a warm laboratory
qs.why: Lina says aquatic animals "spend their lives in water."

qs.q: Which sentence shows how Dad helped Lina stay warm?
choices: Her dad put a thermometer under her tongue to measure her temperature.
On a snowy Saturday, Lina woke up with a scratchy throat.
He turned the thermostat up two degrees and brought her a thermal blanket.
She pulled out a graphic biography about a famous scientist.
qs.why: Raising the heat and bringing a blanket are the two things Dad does to keep her warm.

ev.text: He turned the thermostat up two degrees and brought her a thermal blanket.

qs.q: How does Dad feel about Lina's illness?
choices: He thinks she needs to see a doctor right away today.
He thinks she is only a little sick and should rest.
He thinks she is pretending so that she can stay home.
He thinks she should go to school anyway if she is careful.
qs.why: He says it is "not a real fever," but he still tells her to stay warm, then later to drink tea and rest.

qs.q: What is this conversation mostly about?
choices: A girl wins a school contest for writing the best biography.
A girl and her dad build a model of an old aqueduct together.
A girl is taken to the hospital because of a very high fever.
A girl rests at home and talks with her dad about science.
qs.why: Lina stays home sick, and the talk moves from her temperature to her book, her love of science, and a planned trip.

clues.text: It tells her whole life in drawings
so they spend their lives in water
the author of this book signed my copy
